records.content_text:
We sometimes use brackets to group terms in algebraic expressions together.

As you know, $2x$ means $2 \times x = x + x$.

If we replace the $x$ with $(x + y)$, then in the same way:

$$
2(x + y) = 2 \times (x + y)
$$

We can use repeated addition to work out any multiplication, so:

$$
2 \times (x + y) = (x + y) + (x + y)
$$

We need to remove the brackets before we can collect the like terms and simplify the expression:

$$
(x + y) + (x + y)=x + y + x + y
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{align}
&\phantom{000}2 \times (x + y) \\
&= (x + y) + (x + y) \\
&= x + y + x + y \\
&= x + x + y + y \\
&= 2x + 2y
\end{align}
$$
